Every confirmation transition names its authoritative TIG evidence per the tig_integration.md §7 mapping table; TIG HTTP acceptance alone is never protocol confirmation (mining_system.md §4.5).

Block-age guardrails are the spike values 60 / 110 / 120 from tig_integration.md §8, recorded under spike.workflow_guardrails in config/tig_integration.json. They are spike safeguards, not permanent constants.
Block heights are invented around the fixtures/tig/v1 anchor (block height 100080, round 834) for cross-fixture coherence; they are not live protocol values.
All IDs are obvious fakes; no credentials, signatures, or real addresses appear anywhere (fixtures/tig/v1/README.md convention).

cases.name: delayed_precommit_confirmation
cases.description: A precommit submission times out with an unknown outcome. The gateway reconciles instead of resubmitting; confirmation arrives blocks later through a read, and the assignment is created only then, with the confirmed settings replacing the proposed ones.
cases.rule: architecture.md §7.3 'On an ambiguous outcome it leaves the intent OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, reconciles against confirmed TIG state, and never blindly duplicates the write'; tig_integration.md §10 (single unresolved precommit lane, match search); tig_integration.md §7 (precommit confirmed = get-benchmarks.precommits entry with non-null state.block_confirmed)
